name: LEAP RDBMS
tagline: Educational DBMS by Richard Leyton that executes relational algebra directly instead of SQL.
description: LEAP is a small relational database management system written in C by Richard Leyton, developed from the mid-1990s as a teaching tool. Rather than SQL, it implements the relational algebra itself: users create relations and combine them with relational-algebra operators (selection, projection, joins and set operations), so students can see exactly how algebraic expressions evaluate. It compiles on common Unix systems, had a precompiled Windows GUI, and was distributed under the GNU GPL via SourceForge, with a 1.2.6 release in 2001 and a final 1.2.6.1 source update in February 2004. It still occasionally appears in database courses but receives no development.
statusNote: Educational project; last release 1.2.6.1 (Feb 2004) and site copyright ends in 2005. No ongoing development.
strengths: Executes relational algebra directly, ideal for teaching theory
Small, readable C codebase under the GPL
Runs on Unix variants and had a Windows GUI build
weaknesses: No transactions, concurrency control or performance features
useCases: Teaching relational algebra in database courses
Experimenting with query evaluation in a tiny codebase
notIdealFor: Any production or application data storage
